bull_bear.body: Regulatory risks, intense competition in the telecom sector
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The credit rating upgrade may lead to lower borrowing costs for the company, improving its financial flexibility
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Debt from banks was reduced across the disclosed quarters from Rs 4,813 Cr (Q1FY25) to Rs 726 Cr (Q4FY26); NCDs were nil through Q2FY26 and stand at Rs 3,271 Cr (Q3FY26) and Rs 3,275 Cr (Q4FY26).
- Cash and cash equivalents were Rs 3,715 Cr at Q4FY26, versus Rs 9,932 Cr at Q4FY25 (as tabulated).
- Credit ratings improved to Crisil A-/Stable (May'26) and ICRA A- (Stable) (Jun'26); the deck cites 'Improved credit rating' as a positioning point.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- Described as a "Formidable wireless player" with "3 decades of Telco expertise", "Strong Promoters" and "Improved credit rating" — Crisil A-/Stable May'26 and ICRA A- (Stable) Jun'26.
- Strategy is anchored on "17-5-5 Network Play": 17 key circles account for ~99% of VIL revenue (and +92% of industry revenue), per quarterly TRAI Financial Reports.
- Deck frames the stated ambitions as 1 SUSTAINED Subscriber Addition, 2 DOUBLE-DIGIT Revenue Growth, 3 THRICE Cash EBITDA in 3 years, supported by brand reappraisal, ARPU growth levers, enterprise scale and service differentiation.
- Industry backdrop is presented as "Growing revenue; Stable market structure" with "3 private players + 1 Government player", ARPU among the lowest globally and data consumption among the highest globally.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Brand] Leveraged a CSK partnership to enhance brand visibility and consumer engagement.
- [Market context] Deck cites overall wireless teledensity over 81% and rural teledensity over 60% (TRAI Subscription Report May 2026) as evidence of low penetration / large market potential, with wireless subscribers ~22x wireline and over 1 Bn wireless subscribers.
- [Market context] Digital adoption cited as 500+ Mn UPI customers powering transactions worth approx. Rs. 1 lakh Cr. daily (NPCI), and 70% of individuals in India using internet as of 2025, up from 20% in 2018 (World Bank).
business.title: Notable from the deck

outlook.body: Stable outlook, indicating a positive outlook for the company's financial health
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

deepdive.thesis: Vodafone Idea Limited has received a credit rating upgrade from ICRA, with its long-term fund-based term loans revised to A- from BBB, and the outlook changed to Stable from Positive, indicating a positive outlook for the company's financial health. The upgrade reflects the company's improving operational and financial performance. However, the telecom sector remains competitive, and the company's ability to sustain its performance will be crucial.

open.item: Company targets 4G population coverage of 90% (from over 84% now) over the next couple of quarters, requiring approximately Rs 4,000 crore of capex for the 84%-to-90% bridge.
Full-year FY26 capex guidance of Rs 7,500-8,000 crore (H1FY26 spent Rs 4,200 crore), funded entirely from internal accruals and existing cash with no external funding required for this capex.

open.horizon: on completion of the planned FY27-FY29 investment
open.item: With the planned investments, 4G population coverage in the 17 key circles is expected to increase to over 95%.
AGR installment is ~Rs 16,000 crore annually (FY26 and FY27); spectrum installment ~Rs 12,000-13,000 crore in FY26 rising to ~Rs 26,000-27,000 crore in FY27, becoming payable after the moratorium.
Smart Metering business aims to deploy 12 million smart metering solutions over the next three years.
The Company is in discussions with lenders to secure long-term funding for a planned capital investment programme of Rs 45,000 crore over FY27 to FY29 to expand a fully competitive network.
The Company has committed to sustained customer addition over the next three years, i.e. by FY29.
The Company has committed to a tripling of Cash EBITDA over the next three years, i.e. by FY29.
The Company has committed to double-digit revenue growth over the next three years, i.e. by FY29.
The Company has planned an investment of Rs 45,000 Cr between FY27 and FY29 to expand 4G coverage and 5G services, bridging the 4G coverage gap with competitors in its 17 key circles.
The Company plans a capital investment programme of Rs 45,000 crore over FY27 to FY29 to support expansion of a fully competitive network, with lender discussions ongoing for long-term funding.
Vi Business plans to deploy 12 million smart metering solutions over the next three years.
The Company aims to bring 4G coverage to all national highways, key state highways, airports and places of tourist interest in the remaining 5 circles.
The Aditya Birla Group committed a further equity infusion of US$500 million through fully convertible instruments to support the Company's funding.
The Company aims to provide seamless 5G coverage to all urban areas.
Company continues rolling out 5G on NSA architecture, with current architecture capable of migrating to SA when the need arises; future capex a mix favoring coverage (4G+5G) plus core/transmission.
Company is developing a 'Dedicated Enterprise Corridor' across Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai, adding over 2 Tbps of new capacity and upgrading data centers.
Company is engaged with both banks and NBFCs for long-term debt/private credit funding; banks may await AGR relief clarity post the recent Supreme Court order before extending long-term funding.
Company remains engaged with lenders to secure long-term debt financing to support the Rs 500-550 billion 3-year capex plan.
Company is expanding its Vi One converged broadband+mobility+OTT proposition beyond 3 circles (Mumbai, Gujarat, Maharashtra) into new markets via ISP partnerships (e.g. Asianet in Kerala).

verdicts.item: Company plans to expand 4G population coverage from ~1 billion to 1.2 billion over the next 18 months, growing 4G sites from ~168,000 to ~215,000 (total unique sites to ~210,000-220,000).
verdicts.note: 4G population coverage over 84% (endeavour to 90%); 'We are at around 197,000 unique sites right now.' Progressing toward the 1.2 billion / 215,000-site plan but not yet reached. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Network capacity is targeted to roughly double (2X) from March 2024 to March 2026 via 5G rollout, 3G refarming and additional 4G carriers.
verdicts.note: 'Our 4G data capacity expanded by over 38%... in September, 2025 as compared to March, 2024.' Progress toward the 2X-by-March-2026 target but well short of doubling. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Reaffirmed Rs 500-550 billion capex over next 3 years for 4G coverage and 5G launch, front-ended (first 18 months significantly higher) toward coverage expansion.
verdicts.note: Rs 500-550bn 3-year capex reaffirmed ('to support our Capex plans of Rs. 500 billion to Rs. 550 billion') but front-ended deployment delayed pending debt funding; actual spend far below pace.

verdicts.item: Company remains in active discussions with lenders to raise INR250 billion fund-based and INR100 billion non-fund-based facilities per its stated fundraising plan.
verdicts.note: 'We remain engaged with lenders to secure the long-term debt financing'; the INR250bn + INR100bn facilities still not raised. Timeline pushed out.

verdicts.item: Management expects the elevated ~4% monthly churn rate (vs peers 2-2.5%) to come down materially in the next few quarters as network investments take effect, moving to net subscriber positive.
verdicts.note: 'over the last couple of quarters, we have been sequentially reducing our churn from 5.2 million to 1.6 million to a 0.5 million last quarter which has increased to a 1 million subscriber loss this qu…

verdicts.item: Company will directly deploy 5G in mid-band instead of investing in 4G TDD capacity where it makes sense, with calibrated 5G deployment based on market/monetization evolution.
verdicts.note: 'we have taken the route of NSA architecture'; 5G expanded per 'customer demand and 5G handset penetration', with monetization 'as and when we see a critical mass'. Calibrated 5G deployment underway; …

verdicts.item: Company targets 4G population coverage of 1.1 billion by March 2025 and 1.2 billion by September 2025.
verdicts.note: 4G population coverage over 84% as of September 2025 with endeavour to reach 90%; management does not confirm the 1.2 billion-by-Sep-2025 milestone was hit. Progress but target not confirmed.

verdicts.item: Rollout of 5G in key geographies will start in Q4FY25.
verdicts.note: 'we initiated the launch of 5G services in Mumbai in Mar'25' (i.e., Q4FY25) and expanded to all 17 circles. 5G rollout in key geographies started as promised.

verdicts.item: Management's gut feel is that the subscriber-loss trajectory should turn around by the end of FY25, driven by network investments, though no exact timeline can be given.
verdicts.note: Subscriber-loss trajectory did not turn positive by end FY25; still '1 million subscriber loss this quarter' (Q2FY26) and management 'cannot really give you a finite timeline on turning positive'.

verdicts.item: Company remains actively engaged (CEO + promoters personally involved) to tie up debt funding for long-term network expansion; closure awaited pending clarity on AGR/government support (debt not contingent on AGR relief per TEV report).
verdicts.note: 'We remain actively engaged with our lenders for tying up debt funding'; closure pending, 'there might be a little bit of a dependency on that [SC order] from the banks when they are looking at extend…

verdicts.item: On track to reach 4G population coverage of 1.1 billion by March 2025 (expand by 30 million in 3 months) with ultimate target of 1.2 billion (~90% coverage).
verdicts.note: 4G population coverage over 84% as of Sept 2025 with 'endeavour is to take it to 90%'. Ultimate 1.2 billion (~90%) coverage still pending 'next couple of quarters'.

verdicts.item: Company plans to take 4G tower count to ~215,000-220,000 (an increase of over 45,000 4G towers since start of investment cycle), with another 13,000 towers to be added by middle of Q1FY26.
verdicts.note: 'We added over 1,500 new unique 4G towers during the quarter'; 'We are at around 197,000 unique sites right now.' Progressing toward but short of the 215,000-220,000 target. [±10% rule]

wtt.summary: 25% guidance hit (6 chains); 4/8 projects on-time; 22% theme consistency (info)
wtt.tone_latest: New CEO's first call strikes a steady, hopeful tone: 5G now in all 17 circles and AGR relief prospects improved by the SC order, but subscriber loss ticked back up to 1M (blamed on seasonality), long-term debt funding still unresolved pending AGR clarity, and management repeatedly declines firm timelines on turnaround, 90% coverage and funding.
